Digest a protein and fragment its peptidoforms

peptidoform_fragments.Rd

Fetch a UniProt entry with its annotated modifications, digest it, and return every peptidoform with its fragment ions, plus a census of which annotations were applied.

Fetches a UniProt entry, applies its annotated modifications, digests it with the named protease, and computes fragment ions for every resulting peptidoform.

Usage

peptidoform_fragments(accession, protease = NULL, dissociation = NULL,
  modifications = TRUE, missed_cleavages = NULL, min_length = NULL, max_length = NULL,
  max_modifications = NULL, max_isoforms = NULL, terminus = NULL, timeout = 300)

Arguments

accession

A UniProt accession, e.g. "P02768" (serum albumin).

protease

A protease name, as mzLib names it. NULL means mzLib's default protease.

Read this if you are coming from MaxQuant or Mascot. The names and what each one cuts are mzLib's. mzLib's "trypsin" cuts after K and R even before proline, and "trypsin|P" does not cut before proline: the P names a residue that prevents the cut. That is the reverse of MaxQuant's and Mascot's Trypsin/P, which ignores the proline rule. On serum albumin the two give 202 and 195 distinct peptides, a small count hiding a large difference: which peptides you get changes wherever K or R precedes a proline (smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1106).

dissociation

"HCD" or "CID" (b and y ions), "ETD", "ECD", and the rest of mzLib's dissociation types. NULL means "HCD": mzLib names no default here, so HCD is the bridge's choice until mzLib names one (smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1488).

"ETD" and "ECD" return the c and z-dot series, c and zDot (radical N-Ca cleavage yields c/z-dot, not the b/y of vibrational activation). mzLib PR #1114 removed the spurious y series ETD used to emit.

modifications

Whether to apply UniProt's annotated modifications.

FALSE gives the bare sequences - a clean control, since the digest's distinct backbones are unchanged and only the modified variants of them go away. The peptidoform count drops a long way; on albumin from 310 to 202.

This once carried a caveat saying FALSE also discarded proteolysis products, so that the peptide list itself changed and albumin lost two signal-peptide peptides (smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib#8). That was true and is no longer: both peptides are present either way, and albumin gives 202 distinct base sequences with modifications on or off.

missed_cleavages

Maximum missed cleavage sites per peptide. NULL means mzLib's default.

min_length

Shortest peptide to keep, in residues. NULL means mzLib's default.

mzLib's default silently discards everything shorter. Albumin goes from 202 distinct sequences at the default to 257 at min_length = 1 - a fifth of the digest lives below it - and histone H3.1 keeps 49 of the 96 peptides, by start and end, that it gives at min_length = 1. If you are looking for a short peptide and not finding it, look here first, and pass min_length = 1 when you mean every peptide.

max_length

Longest peptide to keep, in residues. NULL means mzLib's default, which is unbounded; 0 asks for no bound.

max_modifications

Maximum modifications considered per peptide. NULL means mzLib's default. Modification isoforms are enumerated combinatorially: histone H3.1's 49 peptides give 2,419 peptidoforms at two modifications and 6,580 at three.

max_isoforms

Maximum modification isoforms (peptidoforms) generated per peptide position. NULL means mzLib's default.

This cap truncates silently. A truncated result and a genuinely short one look identical from the outside - on histone H3.1 at four modifications the default cap keeps 8,644 of 12,808 peptidoforms, losing about a third. Check digest_truncated before treating a peptide list as exhaustive.

terminus

Which terminus to fragment: "N", "C", "Both" or "None". NULL means mzLib's default.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

The defaults are mzLib's, not this package's. Every digestion option you leave as NULL is not sent, and mzLib's own default (its DigestionParams) applies; the Parameters table below gives each value at the pinned mzLib. mzLib names no default dissociation type, so the bridge uses HCD until it does (smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1488). The result says which protease, dissociation type, terminus and caps were used.

Value

An mzlibr_digest: a list with the scalars describing the run, a census (see census_explain), and three data.frames that join on peptide_index - peptides, fragments and modifications.

The scalars: sequence_length, the protein's length in residues; protease, dissociation and terminus, each the one passed or the default used; max_modifications, the cap in modifications per peptidoform, and max_modification_isoforms, the cap in peptidoforms per peptide position, each the value passed or mzLib's default; peptides_at_isoform_cap, the peptide positions that reached it - non-zero means the list is truncated; and min_length and max_length in residues and missed_cleavages in cleavage sites, as passed, or NA when left to mzLib, since the bridge does not report those three back. The census counts sites in residues (distinct positions carrying a modification), applied in modifications and annotated in UniProt features.

peptides has monoisotopic_mass, the neutral mass in Da; length in residues; missed_cleavages in cleavage sites; modification_count in modifications; and fixed_charges, the formal charge the intact peptide carries before protonation.

peptides holds peptidoforms, not distinct sequences. One row per sequence-and-modification-placement, so albumin's default digest is 310 rows over 202 distinct sequences. Both are legitimate answers to "how many peptides" and they are not interchangeable; quoting one for the other is a large error, not a rounding one. See digest_distinct_base_sequences.

Wraps

Wire verb peptidoform fragments. Generated from the bridge's verb spec peptidoform.fragments.yaml (bridge commit 22638d4276ff) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • Loaders.LoadUniprot in mzLib/UsefulProteomicsDatabases/Loaders.cs at mzLib 23c2490e

  • Protein.Digest in mzLib/Proteomics/Protein/Protein.cs at mzLib 23c2490e

  • DigestionParams in mzLib/Proteomics/ProteolyticDigestion/DigestionParams.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • ProteaseDictionary in mzLib/Proteomics/ProteolyticDigestion/ProteaseDictionary.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • proteases.tsv (each protease name's cleavage motif) in mzLib/Proteomics/ProteolyticDigestion/proteases.tsv at mzLib d10017ce

  • PeptideWithSetModifications.Fragment in mzLib/Proteomics/ProteolyticDigestion/PeptideWithSetModifications.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

accession

string; required. A UniProtKB accession, e.g. P02768; fetched from rest.uniprot.org. The bridge checks only that it is not blank (the bindings upper-case it and check its shape first). UniProt's 400 or 404 becomes a usage error.

protease

string; default absent; range a key of mzLib's ProteaseDictionary. mzLib protease name. Absent, the bridge sends none and DigestionParams' default applies ("trypsin" at d10017ce). The names and what each one cuts are mzLib's, defined in proteases.tsv. At d10017ce "trypsin" is K|,R|, which cuts after K and R even before P; "trypsin|P" is K[P]|,R[P]|, where [P] marks a residue that prevents the cut, so it does not cut before P. These are not MaxQuant's or Mascot's names: their "Trypsin/P" ignores the proline rule. On serum albumin (P02768) "trypsin" gives 202 distinct peptides and "trypsin|P" gives 195 (other options absent).

dissociation

string; default HCD; range a mzLib DissociationType name, case-insensitive: HCD, CID, ETD, EThcD, .... Which fragment series to generate: HCD and CID give b and y; ETD gives c and zDot. Absent, HCD. mzLib's Fragment requires a type and names no default, so HCD is the bridge's own stop-gap until mzLib names one. mzLib#1488 asks for HCD, which MetaMorpheus's CommonParameters already defaults to.

terminus

string; default absent; range a mzLib FragmentationTerminus name, case-insensitive: Both, N, C. Which fragment termini to generate. It is also passed to DigestionParams. Absent, DigestionParams' default applies (Both at d10017ce), to the digest and to the fragments.

modifications (wire --no-modifications)

flag; default FALSE. Digest the bare sequence: UniProt's modifications are discarded but its signal-peptide and propeptide boundaries are kept (pyMzLib#8), so the backbone peptide list is unchanged and only the modified variants go away. A clean control.

missed_cleavages (wire --missed-cleavages)

int; in cleavage sites; default absent; range >= 0. Maximum missed cleavage sites per peptide (DigestionParams maxMissedCleavages). Absent, DigestionParams' default applies (2 at d10017ce).

min_length (wire --min-length)

int; in residues; default absent; range >= 1. Shortest peptide kept (DigestionParams minPeptideLength). Absent, DigestionParams' default applies (7 at d10017ce). That default drops shorter peptides silently: histone H3.1 (P68431) keeps 49 of the 96 peptides it gives at 1 (distinct start and end, other options absent). Pass 1 for every peptide.

max_length (wire --max-length)

int; in residues; default absent; range >= 0. Longest peptide kept (DigestionParams maxPeptideLength); 0 means unbounded. Absent, DigestionParams' default applies (unbounded at d10017ce).

max_modifications (wire --max-mods)

int; in modifications; default absent; range >= 0. Maximum modifications per peptidoform (DigestionParams maxModsForPeptides). Absent, DigestionParams' default applies (2 at d10017ce). Isoforms grow combinatorially: histone H3.1's 49 peptides give 2,419 peptidoforms at 2 and 6,580 at 3, where 2 peptide positions already reach the isoform cap (other options absent).

max_isoforms (wire --max-isoforms)

int; in peptidoforms; default absent; range >= 1. Cap on modification isoforms per peptide position (DigestionParams maxModificationIsoforms). Absent, DigestionParams' default applies (1024 at d10017ce). mzLib truncates SILENTLY at the cap; peptides_at_isoform_cap reports it.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

accession

string; never NA. The accession UniProt returned.

name

string; NA when the entry records no entry name. UniProt entry name, e.g. ALBU_HUMAN.

full_name

string; NA when the entry records no recommended name. Recommended protein name, e.g. Albumin.

organism

string; NA when the entry records no organism. Scientific name.

sequence_length

int; in residues; never NA. Length of the full precursor sequence.

modifications_applied

bool; never NA. False under no-modifications.

census$sites (wire annotated_modification_sites)

int; in residues; never NA. Distinct residue positions carrying at least one loaded modification. Not a modification count: K9me1/me2/me3/ac are four modifications at one site.

census$applied (wire annotated_modifications_loaded)

int; in modifications; never NA. Modifications mzLib loaded onto the protein (summed over sites). Counted from the annotated entry, so unchanged by no-modifications.

census$annotated (wire uniprot_annotated_features)

int; in features; never NA. Modification-like features in the XML: modified residue, glycosylation site, lipid moiety-binding region and cross-link.

census$unresolved (wire unresolved_modifications)

string[]; never NA. Modification names the entry annotates that could not be resolved against UniProt's ptmlist, sorted. These are dropped silently by mzLib otherwise.

census$by_type (wire uniprot_features_by_type)

object[]; never NA. {type, count, loaded} per feature type, sorted by type. loaded is true only for 'modified residue' and 'lipid moiety-binding region': mzLib drops the others on feature TYPE alone, before any mass lookup.

protease

string; never NA. The protease used: the one given, or DigestionParams' default.

dissociation

string; never NA. DissociationType name used: the one given, or HCD.

terminus

string; never NA. FragmentationTerminus name used: the one given, or DigestionParams' default.

max_modifications

int; in modifications; never NA. max-mods as used: the value given, or DigestionParams' default.

max_modification_isoforms

int; in peptidoforms; never NA. max-isoforms as used: the value given, or DigestionParams' default.

peptides_at_isoform_cap

int; in peptide positions; never NA. Peptide positions (start, end) whose peptidoforms in mzLib's raw digest, counted before the bridge collapses the mzLib#1108 duplicates, reached max-isoforms. Non-zero means the list is TRUNCATED.

peptide_count

int; in peptidoforms; never NA. Entries in peptides.

peptides

object[]; never NA. One entry per distinct peptidoform (start, end, full sequence), in digestion order; fields under result.columns.

Columns of peptides

base_sequence

string; never NA. Bare residues.

full_sequence

string; never NA. mzLib full sequence with modifications inline, e.g. ...K[UniProt:N6-succinyllysine on K].

monoisotopic_mass

float; in Da; never NA. Neutral monoisotopic mass, modifications included.

length

int; in residues; never NA. Peptide length.

one_based_start

int; never NA. First residue's position in the protein, 1-based.

one_based_end

int; never NA. Last residue's position in the protein, 1-based, inclusive.

missed_cleavages

int; in cleavage sites; never NA. Missed cleavage sites spanned.

modification_count

int; in modifications; never NA. Entries in modifications.

fixed_charges

int; in charge; never NA. Formal charges the INTACT peptide carries before protonation (e.g. trimethyllysine's quaternary ammonium), recovered from each modification's formula-vs-recorded mass deficit in whole electrons. m/z at charge z is (monoisotopic_mass + (z - fixed_charges) * 1.00727646677) / z. Does NOT apply to fragments.

modifications

object[]; never NA. {one_based_residue, terminus, id, mass, formal_charge} per modification: one_based_residue is 1-based within the PEPTIDE and null for a terminal modification, which sets terminus 'N' or 'C' instead (terminus is null for a residue modification); id is mzLib's IdWithMotif; mass is its monoisotopic mass in Da, never null for a loaded modification (mzLib keeps one only if it has a formula or a mass, and fills a missing mass from the formula); formal_charge in elementary charges.

fragments

object[]; never NA. {product_type, fragment_number, neutral_mass, neutral_loss, residue_position} per ion: product_type e.g. b, y, c, zDot; fragment_number the position in its series; neutral_mass the monoisotopic NEUTRAL mass in Da (not an m/z; no proton added); neutral_loss in Da (0 when none); residue_position 1-based within the peptide.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

accession missing or blank; UniProt answers 400 or 404 (no such entry); the entry holds no protein sequence; protease not in ProteaseDictionary; dissociation or terminus not an enum name; an integer option that is not an integer

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

UniProt unreachable by the bridge's own classification: a timeout (HttpClient 100 s), a socket or TLS failure, a request that never got a response, an HTTP 408, 429 or 5xx, or a body cut off in transit

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

any other UniProt status (e.g. 403); UniProt's ptmlist.txt or PSI-MOD.obo.xml missing from the bridge payload (FileNotFoundException: every protein would otherwise look unmodified or carry wrong charges); mzLib failing to parse the entry or to digest it

Caveats

  • UniProt annotates more than mzLib applies: only 'modified residue' and 'lipid moiety-binding region' features load. Serum albumin: 14 of 38 annotated features applied, the 24 glycosylation-site features dropped on type (mzLib#1112). Read uniprot_features_by_type and unresolved_modifications before trusting a modification count.

  • max-isoforms truncates silently in mzLib. Histone H3.1 at four modifications keeps 8,644 of its 12,808 peptidoforms at the default cap of 1024, losing about a third. Check peptides_at_isoform_cap before treating the list as exhaustive.

  • Duplicate peptidoforms that mzLib's Digest emits where a chain boundary meets the initiator-Met cleavage site (mzLib#1108, open) are collapsed by the bridge on (start, end, full sequence).

  • Fragment masses are neutral. Converting one to m/z needs the fixed charge within that fragment's span, which the wire does not report; fixed_charges is whole-peptide only.

  • ETD's zDot ions are suppressed N-terminal to proline while the complementary c ions are not, leaving about 4% of the c series unobservable (mzLib#1110).

  • Needs the network: UniProt is queried on every call.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.peptidoform.fragments

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::peptidoform::fragments_with with FragmentOptions

  • R (mzLibR): peptidoform_fragments

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.1.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • Integer options are not range-checked by the bridge (negative min-length, max-isoforms 0); the bindings check them, not alike (min_length 0 passes pyMzLib and mzLibRust, not mzLibR). Enum.TryParse also accepts numeric strings: --dissociation 3 passes as SID, and --dissociation 99 or --terminus 7 pass as undefined members. mzLib's behaviour on those values is unverified.

  • The envelope echoes the protease, dissociation, terminus and both caps it used, but not missed-cleavages, min-length or max-length. Since 2026-10-21 those can be mzLib's defaults, so a binding cannot show the values used (mzLibR prints NA as 'mzLib's default'). Echoing them, read from the DigestionParams the bridge built, would be additive and optional (CONTRACT.md).

  • Unmeasured: mzLib caps isoforms per proteolytic peptide (ProteolyticPeptide.cs:62), so a position that two proteolysis products both produce (the mzLib#1108 duplicates) is capped twice but counted once. It could then read as at the cap when neither copy was cut.

References

  • doi:10.1093/nar/gkae1010: UniProt, the source of the entry, its sequence and its annotated modifications (UniProt Consortium 2025, NAR)

See also

digest_fragments_by_series, digest_truncated, peptide_mz

Examples


digest <- peptidoform_fragments("P02768", max_modifications = 1)
digest
#> <mzlibr_digest> P02768 ALBU_HUMAN (Homo sapiens)
#>   609 residues, trypsin, HCD, terminus Both
#>   min_length mzLib's default, missed cleavages mzLib's default, max 1 modifications
#>   2 peptidoforms over 2 distinct sequences
#>   128 fragments: b=64, y=64
#>   ! 14 of 38 annotated modifications applied. See ?census_explain.
head(digest$peptides[, c("base_sequence", "monoisotopic_mass", "modification_count")])
#>                         base_sequence monoisotopic_mass modification_count
#> 1     ALVLIAFAQYLQQCPFEDHVKLVNEVTEFAK          3562.853                  0
#> 2 RPCFSALEVDETYVPKEFNAETFTFHADICTLSEK          4136.902                  1
digest_fragments_by_series(digest)
#>   product_type  n
#> 1            b 64
#> 2            y 64
